\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{रैवणो} (raivṇo)}{रैवणो (raivṇo)}]{\mw{रैवणो} (raivṇo) — to stay, to live}

\label{lesson:MW-C105-raivno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to ask for, then the Marwadi for to look.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{रैवणो}}
\textbf{\mw{रैवणो}} — \emph{raivṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to stay, to live\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{रैवणो}} (\emph{raivṇo}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*rahati}, \textquotedblleft{}remains\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants. CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{rahaï} under it (CDIAL 10666).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raivṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{raivṇo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to ask for, then the Marwadi for to look, then say \emph{raivṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{बांचणो} (bā̃chṇo)}{बांचणो (bā̃chṇo)}]{\mw{बांचणो} (bā̃chṇo) — to read}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to look, then the Marwadi for to stay.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{बांचणो}}
\textbf{\mw{बांचणो}} — \emph{bā̃chṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to read\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{बांचणो}} (\emph{bā̃chṇo}) is usually linked with Sanskrit \emph{vācayati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to say, reads\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL follows into Prakrit \emph{vāyēi}, \textquotedblleft{}reads\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 11471), but not into Marwari or Hindi. That entry does not explain the nasal and the \emph{ch} of \textbf{\mw{बांचणो}} (\emph{bā̃chṇo}), so the link is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}
